Define a Skat ruleset

Source: R/ruleset.R
sk_ruleset.Rd

Builds a configuration object describing which rule variant to use. Two presets cover the common cases: official tournament rules as used by the German Skat federation (DSkV) and the International Skat Players Association (ISPA), and a relaxed casual ("Kneipe") variant. Individual options can be overridden. This is descriptive metadata: play and scoring functions do not consume this object. Bock, Ramsch and Kontra/Re game flows are not implemented.

Usage

sk_ruleset(
  preset = c("tournament", "casual"),
  bock = FALSE,
  ramsch = NULL,
  contra_re = NULL,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

Arguments

preset

One of "tournament" or "casual". Sets sensible defaults for the remaining options.

bock

Logical; whether Bock rounds (doubled scores) are in effect. Only meaningful for "casual"; ignored in scoring unless enabled. Defaults to FALSE.

ramsch

Logical; whether a passed-in deal is played as Ramsch rather than thrown in. Casual only. Defaults to the preset.

contra_re

Logical; whether Kontra/Re announcements are permitted. Casual only. Defaults to the preset.

call

The calling environment, used for error reporting.

Value

An object of class sk_ruleset: a list with the logical elements preset, bock, ramsch, and contra_re.

See also

is_sk_ruleset() to test an object.

Other ruleset functions: is_sk_ruleset()

Examples

sk_ruleset("tournament")
#> <sk_ruleset> ("tournament")
#> • Bock rounds: FALSE
#> • Ramsch on pass: FALSE
#> • Kontra/Re: FALSE
sk_ruleset("casual", bock = TRUE)
#> <sk_ruleset> ("casual")
#> • Bock rounds: TRUE
#> • Ramsch on pass: TRUE
#> • Kontra/Re: TRUE
